newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures ease with cash market.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures ease with cash market.

text.p: IPE Brent futures eased on Monday in sympathy with a weakening Brent crude cash market, but traders said volume was very light.
December Brent was trading 12 cents down at $24.10 a barrel at 1244 GMT.
"It's just following the cash. The Dec/Jan spread's come in and basically we're just following that," one trader said.

Dated Brent extended the descent set in motion on Friday after Shell Trading (Stasco), which inflated prices for most of last week with the purchase of some seven cargoes, showed no interest in buying further cargoes.
A physical cargo of Brent traded on Friday at November Brent -20 cents, down some 32 cents from Thursday.
Offers on the Dec/Jan spread, which went as high as 63 cents during the morning have now fallen to 54 cents.
"Also to be honest, Brent's close on Friday was pretty inflated, so we're just retracing that a bit," the trader added.
Gas oil was slightly firmer, trading $1.0 higher at $225.75 a tonne. Traders said it had been encouraged by heating oil's apparent recovery on NYMEX on Friday.
November heating oil closed 1.23 cents a gallon higher at 71.12 cents on Friday. It was trading at the same level on ACCESS at 1244 GMT.
A number of traders said the market was already looking ahead to American Petroleum Institute data due out on Tuesday.
"It may appear a long way off but in the present climate they taken on more importance than usual," one trader said. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714
